document: Group B approval — snapshot and causality
approval_source: Explicit owner reply: 'aprovo' to the Group B approval request, including Option A for BUF-001.

approved_decisions.approved_rule: Each match freezes an immutable definition manifest with catalog, effect registry, balance rules and ruleset release IDs plus a verifiable content digest. Each CardInstance stores a resolved mechanical definition snapshot and per-definition digest. schema_version remains structural only.

Use a UUIDv4 operation_id for each logical action and separate UUIDv4 event_id values for domain events. Events are ordered, append-only and causally linked. Same operation_id plus same fingerprint replays the stored result; conflicting fingerprint reuse rejects. Updated state, revision, operation result and generated events commit atomically.

Rarity is classification only. It does not modify effect magnitude, thresholds, target count/selection, duration or other execution parameters. RARITY_EFFECT_BUDGET must not exist as an execution dependency in the new system.
Reactive effects have their own source_effect_id and causal parent. They never inherit rarity or execution parameters from the external effect that triggered them.
Only active, verified catalog bindings become capabilities in the new effect registry. Orphan handlers and inactive aliases remain historical/compatibility records until explicitly rebound.

A successful removal/sacrifice produces its removal event. A separate Vengeance event may follow only when the target has Vengeance and the Group F cause policy permits that cause. A shield-blocked attempt is not a removal and does not trigger Vengeance.

Rykard's reactive Vengeance output and direct leader output are separate events with their own sources and order. The legacy +1 and +2 are recorded as observed outputs; the aggregate +3 is not frozen as a final balance value.

explicit_non_approvals: The complete numeric balance model, rarity cutoffs, EFP, deck cost, deck budget 32 and leader_load remain unapproved.
The final list of removal/sacrifice causes that permit Vengeance remains a Group F decision.
Group C state duration and cleanup policies, Group D target/atomic action policies and Group E database/CAS implementation remain open.
No runtime code, active catalog, database schema, API or frontend is authorized to change by this approval alone.
